intro.title: Cart Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a shopping cart context to manage product data and cart state across your Vue application. You'll learn how to use Vue's Composition API, specifically the `ref` and `provide`/`inject` functions, to create and share reactive state. This involves creating a centralized cart context that holds items and provides methods to add or remove them. By the end, you'll have a functional cart system that demonstrates state management in a beginner-friendly Vue project.
intro.usecase: Cart context is a fundamental pattern in e-commerce applications where multiple components need access to shared shopping cart data. You'll see this in product listings, cart summary widgets, checkout flows, and header cart indicators - all needing to display consistent cart information without prop drilling. For example, when a user adds an item from a product card, the cart icon in the navigation bar should immediately update the item count. This pattern also enables features like persistent carts across page navigation and real-time inventory synchronization across different UI sections.
